steps.text: The practice strokes give a useful pressure range: about 3 mm of press makes a 2.7 mm line, and 10 mm makes an 11.3 mm line. Deep stationary presses also make large blobs, so I’ll bring the brush into contact while moving and taper it out along each stroke.

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import PchipInterpolator
S=.227185/1024
Q=[0,1,0,0]
def pose(u,v,z,practice=False):return [-.1+(511.5-v)*S,(-.1856+(223.5-u)*S) if practice else (511.5-u)*S,z]+Q

def samples(knots,step=1.5):
 a=np.array(knots,float);t=np.r_[0,np.cumsum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(a[:,:2],axis=0),axis=1))]
 tt=np.linspace(0,t[-1],int(t[-1]/step)+1)
 return np.array([PchipInterpolator(t,a[:,i])(tt) for i in range(3)]).T

def stroke(knots,offset=(0,0),practice=False,speed=10,lead=0):
 a=samples(knots,step=speed*.05/(S*1000));a[:,:2]+=offset
 # steady moving brush width observed on practice, mm.
 width=a[:,2]*S*1000;dep=np.interp(width,[0,.49,2.7,6.37,11.28,16.92],[.65,1,3,6,10,15])/1000

 rows=[approach]*8+rows
 last=rows[-1];rows+=[[last[0],last[1],z]+Q for z in np.linspace(last[2],.045,16)]
 cmd.append({'op':'rows','rows':rows,'note':'brush stroke along exemplar length'})
 return cmd
